title: Design note: land each job directly on host main, not a local branch
summary: Write a design note under docs/design/ for throughput review 20261110-024838-mch9: stop using the long-lived local landing branch as a staging area. Build each verified job's landing commit directly on host main (merge_tree then commit_tree) and push it. The note states the predicted saving of 5.0 minutes per landed job and how the next throughput review measures it. Audience: Athena maintainers and the next throughput review.

A criterion requires the measurement method against the 5.0 minute prediction.

assumptions: Goal: a written design (no code) for maintainers and the next throughput review. The request's truncated text is completed from its stated proposed change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new file under docs/design/ cites throughput review 20261110-024838-mch9 and quotes the measured 2203.6 of 2252.0 median minutes per landed job from THROUGHPUT.md.

The note explains how the change removes the bottleneck: the verified job's single landing commit is built on current host main via Git::merge_tree from the job's recorded base, then Git::commit_tree, then pushed, so the local landing branch is no longer a staging area. It says why the stage's wait (the later of the outcome and the newest landing record) shrinks.

The note states the predicted saving of 5.0 minutes per landed job and says how the next throughput review measures it: it compares the landing-and-rebuild minutes measured after the change landed with this prediction.

The note has alternatives considered, risks and rollback sections. It has an Existing code section that reuses or extends docs/design/per-job-main-landing.md, docs/design/per-job-landing-branches.md, crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs and crates/athena-core/src/land.rs by path, and states what differs from them.
The note says that a change implementing the design must cite throughput review 20261110-024838-mch9 in its request text.

out_of_scope: Editing existing design notes beyond a link
